lead: you said it to him plainly at twenty-two, and neither of you has had to repeat it since. the last new thing you learned about your oldest friend, he volunteered, somewhere in the third year.
sun: what you gave him does not run on interest, and that is the whole of its strength here. you would be on a train tonight, for anything, at any hour, and both of you know it without having to check. the terms were set in one conversation and have needed nothing since — no renewal, no evidence, no season in which they came up for review.
moon: The Blaze is a faculty for the unfound, and it has nothing to do here. it goes out every year toward people you met last month, and they get the full apparatus: the questions, the following-up, the two hours of close attention. he was finished being unknown before either of you had a mortgage, and nothing has pointed at him since.
pull: you would give him a kidney and you have not asked him a real question in nine years, and both of those are the same arrangement doing what it does.
tension: he can see it. he watches you take a new person apart over one dinner, with real interest, and he has not had that from you since his twenties. he is not owed it — nothing was ever promised about interest. what he has instead is somebody nothing could remove, and if he ever put the complaint into words the honest reply would be structural rather than warm, and he would hear the difference immediately.
cost: people bring you what they cannot say elsewhere, having recognised across one table that you are not losable. the oldest ones, though, are held by an instrument that never required you to find them interesting. none has been examined in twenty years, and any of them could have become a different person in that time without your noticing.

lead: four minutes on your feet in a full room, at the volume it came out at, and then eleven years of sitting down at that same table every quarter with the same people, saying nothing about it.
sun: you were not defending yourself. you had given your word to somebody who was not in the building, years before, and the afternoon arrived when keeping it meant saying a name out loud in front of everybody. the standing up was terms operating. and the room you did it in belongs to an arrangement you entered on purpose and will still be inside at sixty.
moon: it came out whole, at the size it was in you, and there is no reduced version available afterwards. the room got the size and none of the reason, because a promise made years earlier in a kitchen is not visible from a chair in a meeting. what stayed on that room was volume with no cause attached.
pull: the four minutes are permanent and so is your seat. you will keep the promise that caused them and keep attending the room that saw them, for another twenty years, in silence.
tension: the correction exists and cannot be issued. explaining that afternoon would mean naming what you had promised and to whom, and the promise only worked unnamed, so the version that stands is that you went off at a colleague over nothing. the man it protected has never learned it happened. the people who watched still work with you, pleasantly, around something nobody has raised in eleven years.
cost: an undertaking of yours will survive being expensive in public, which is unusual enough that two people have built their working lives on the assumption. the same construction gives that afternoon nowhere to go. a scene inside something with an exit gets left behind when you leave; yours happened inside an arrangement with no leaving in it, so it sits in the room at full size, every quarter, indefinitely.

lead: eleven years after she walked out of the partnership without notice, she came back expecting a negotiation. her name had never come off the door, and the terms the two of you set at the start were still running.
sun: removing her would have taken an act, and no act was available to you. there was no meeting at which the question got put, no year in which it came up, because what the two of you agreed at twenty-nine was entered rather than arranged, and a thing entered does not lapse from disuse. eleven years of her absence changed the workload and changed nothing about the terms.
moon: The Return does not file anybody as gone, and it never presents itself as hope — the part of you that would have registered a departure simply did not register one. the eleven years were not endured, then. they were the interval before the ordinary thing happened, and when she came through the door your body treated it as a tuesday.
pull: she came back to be forgiven and found nothing on the books to forgive. the arrangement had gone on being kept by one of you, without strain, and without anybody deciding to.
tension: what she wanted was an account of the eleven years — what they cost you, some evidence that her going had landed somewhere. you cannot produce one, because it did not land. the grievance was never opened and cannot be opened retrospectively, and telling her the truth of it, that her absence was absorbed without difficulty, is worse than any bill you could hand her. so she has come home to a welcome she cannot feel.
cost: two other people have organised their working lives around you as a fixed point, on the evidence that arrangements here survive their own members leaving. nothing can be ended by stopping, though. her eleven years of silence were not a resignation, and neither is anything you could do now, and the pair of you are still in it at fifty.

lead: he asked you in a car park, not a hospital, four years before he got ill, and you said yes the way you would to anything. twelve years dead now, and the yes is still in operation.
sun: an agreement between two people needs both of them to change it, and one of them is not available, so the terms stand exactly as they were spoken. there has been no review, no adjustment for the fact that his daughter is thirty-one now and his widow remarried. you have gone on executing a sentence agreed in a car park by two men in their forties, one of whom is twelve years gone.
moon: what actually goes out has no figure on it. the calls, the fees, the two weeks every year — nothing meters any of it, and at any remove it looks like soft, formless devotion, a grief that never closed. up close it is a set of terms being executed, competently, by somebody who is not sad most days and turns up anyway.
pull: the only person who could release you from it is the one who asked. nothing about that has been negotiable since the funeral, and nothing about it has ever needed to be said aloud.
tension: the family think it is love, and say so warmly, and the accurate version — that he asked, you agreed, and the agreement has been running that household ever since — would land in the room as a coldness and would also be news, since nobody alive was there for it. you let them keep the warm account. it leaves one witness to an undertaking that currently governs four other lives, and that witness is you.
cost: a dead man's arrangements get honoured here at exactly the rate a living man's would, which is rare — the dead cannot check, and most undertakings slacken quietly at that point. yours did not register the difference. nothing can conclude it, either: no completion, no discharge, nobody left with standing to say it is enough. the calls still go out on the old schedule.
